scene.label: Interactive 3D lesson network showing SBD-SPLUNK01 patching from SBD-REPO01, receiving the collector’s two streams from SBD-SYSLOG01 over TLS, and serving the administration seats, with one test event traced from SBD-DC01 through the collector to Splunk and SBD-AUDIT01.
scene.completeCaption: SBD-SPLUNK01 holds a working copy of the collector’s record, answers three searches, and raises alerts with named responders. One failed sign-in on SBD-DC01 has been traced to the collector, the analyst’s screen, and the repository’s archive.

nodes.name: SBD-SPLUNK01
nodes.title: SBD-SPLUNK01 · 10.0.50.10
nodes.description: The analysis server, a single Splunk instance built in lesson 1 on domain-joined Linux, patched only from SBD-REPO01, and hardened to DISA’s Splunk Enterprise STIG in lesson 3. It indexes a working copy of the collector’s streams for searches and alerts; the protected record stays on SBD-AUDIT01.

nodes.name: SBD-SYSLOG01
nodes.title: SBD-SYSLOG01 · 10.0.20.20
nodes.description: The collector from course 1.3. Lesson 2 adds a universal forwarder that reads its two streams — the ForwardedEvents log and the per-sender syslog files — and sends them to SBD-SPLUNK01 over TLS under rule F10.

nodes.name: SBD-AUDIT01
nodes.title: SBD-AUDIT01 · 10.0.50.40
nodes.description: The repository from course 1.4, kept out of the analysis flow. Its findings become alerts in lesson 5, and lesson 6 finds the traced event in its next-morning archive.

nodes.name: SBD-DC01
nodes.title: SBD-DC01 · 10.0.10.10
nodes.description: The PDC emulator and the domain’s time source. SBD-SPLUNK01 takes its time from the domain controllers and joins sbd.test in lesson 1, and lesson 6’s test event starts here.

nodes.name: SBD-REPO01
nodes.title: SBD-REPO01 · 10.0.70.20
nodes.description: The Linux repository from course 1.2: SBD-SPLUNK01’s only source of operating-system packages over rule F19, configured before its first update.

nodes.name: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01
nodes.title: SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 · 10.0.60.20
nodes.description: The Tier 1 seat. The host’s administrators reach SBD-SPLUNK01 over SSH from here, and analysts sign in to Splunk Web from here (rule A02).

nodes.name: AdminJumpBox01
nodes.title: AdminJumpBox01 · 10.0.60.10
nodes.description: The Tier 0 seat. The alerts that watch the domain controllers are changed from here (rule A01), and the tier-account lookup is exported here from course 1.1’s groups.

flows.label: SSH and Splunk Web · rule A02

chapters.network: SBD-SPLUNK01 comes up on VLAN 50, patched from SBD-REPO01 over rule F19 and administered over SSH from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01. It takes its time from the domain controllers and joins sbd.test; nothing is indexed yet.
The forwarder on SBD-SYSLOG01 now sends the forwarded Windows events and the syslog files to SBD-SPLUNK01 over TLS on TCP 9997 (rule F10). SBD-AUDIT01 stays out of this flow by design.

Nothing new crosses the network. SBD-SPLUNK01 keeps receiving over rule F10 while its console, accounts, and storage are hardened from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 (rule A02), and only Splunk Web, the receiving port, and SSH stay open to other hosts.

Analysts reach Splunk Web over HTTPS from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01 (rule A02) and search the working copy that the forwarder keeps current over rule F10, including the core router’s deny log, which reaches the collector under rule F24.

SBD-SPLUNK01 now watches its stream for privileged failures, boundary denies, time faults, silent sources, and the repository’s findings. The alerts on the domain controllers are changed from AdminJumpBox01 (rule A01).

Every flow is shown: SBD-DC01’s test event reaches SBD-SYSLOG01, which forwards it to SBD-SPLUNK01 within seconds and archives it to SBD-AUDIT01 the next morning, while analysts watch from SBD-ADMIN-SRV01.
